goal: Record the first Flexus-vs-gem5 timing comparison phase on multi-core snapshot_0, including the canonical run_sample interface bring-up, the gem5 MAIR restore fix, the remaining IPC gap, and the structural mismatches intentionally deferred to later phases.

confirmed_fix.summary: Resynchronized MAIR_EL1 backing registers during ISA unserialize so page walks and restored misc-reg state agree.

major_findings: Flexus and gem5 now share the same canonical run_sample reporting contract.
The gem5 MAIR restore bug was real and materially improved correctness and performance once fixed.
The dominant remaining gem5 delay is in the Ruby request-service path, not post-response retire handling.
The first 4-slice gem5 step did not improve IPC because gem5 currently homes slices on low bits above the cache-line offset, which collapses this workload onto slice 0.
Flexus uses 4KB L2 group interleaving, so gem5 and Flexus are still not structurally matched at the LLC homing level.
deferred_work: Add or approximate Flexus-like LLC slice homing in gem5 Ruby.
Move gem5 from crossbar to mesh after the slicing/homing semantics are settled.
Repeat the canonical microbenchmark after those structural changes and reassess the remaining IPC gap.
